target.title: Draft: add commands list and inspect inventory
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a read-only operator/developer command inventory:

```text
openclaw commands list [--json|--markdown] [--plugin-descriptors]
openclaw commands inspect <command-path...> [--json|--markdown] [--plugin-descriptors]
```

This is the recommended initial implementation from [Command Catalog RFC #32](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/32). It joins command information OpenClaw already owns so compliance, diagnostics, documentation, policy tooling, and future scoped prompt consumers do not each rebuild the same registry joins.

## Scope

`commands list` joins existing command-owned sources:

- static CLI descriptors
- command routes and routed operations
- the current Commander tree
- opt-in plugin CLI descriptors
- caller-supplied node command declarations

`commands inspect` hydrates the requested lazy core/sub-CLI group, resolves runtime aliases, and joins exact command records with inherited route and routed-operation metadata.

This draft does not add ownerless tool adapters, aggregate audit/test/summary commands, prompt generation, generated docs, or a new execution path. Node records are supported in the object model but no live `node.list` / `node.describe` bridge is claimed yet.

## Plugin contract and failure behavior

Plugin descriptors may optionally report `effectProfile`, `commandExposure`, and `hidden`. Their values, defaults, and non-enforcement semantics are documented in `docs/plugins/sdk-overview.md` with an external-plugin example.

When `--plugin-descriptors` is requested, loader exceptions or error-level plugin diagnostics now fail the command. They cannot produce an apparently valid incomplete inventory. Warnings remain visible without invalidating successful results.

## Existing Gateway surface

OpenClaw already has Gateway RPC `commands.list` for agent-facing chat/native/skill/plugin commands. This CLI adds an operator/developer inventory; it does not replace or change the Gateway RPC. Future convergence remains an explicit RFC decision.

## Review layers

- [PR1: commands list](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/24)
- [PR2: commands inspect and ClawSweeper hardening](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/25)
- [Optional PR3: scoped prompt projection](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/26)

## Real behavior proof

Exact head: `90a7b1ca2b`

Core-only inventory, using an isolated state directory:

```text
schemaVersion=1
commandDescriptors=61
runtimeCommands=26
pluginCommands=0
```

Opt-in plugin inventory, also isolated:

```json
{"schemaVersion":1,"commandDescriptors":61,"runtimeCommands":26,"pluginCommands":3,"pluginIds":"browser:browser,canvas:nodes canvas,memory-core:memory"}
```

Controlled plugin registration failure:

```json
{"exitCode":1,"stdoutBytes":0,"errorMatched":true}
```

The failure fixture throws during plugin registration. The command emits no JSON document and exits nonzero with `Failed to load plugin CLI descriptor metadata` on stderr.

## Validation

- 44 focused inventory tests from the promoted PR1+PR2 stack
- latest hardening rerun: 10 focused CLI/metadata tests passed
- source execution proved core-only, plugin-enabled, and plugin-failure paths
- `git diff --check`
- clean final Codex review after the ClawSweeper fixes

The full local core TypeScript runner did not complete within two five-minute attempts on this worktree; it emitted no diagnostics. Focused Vitest compilation and runtime source execution passed.

## Feedback requested

Is `openclaw commands` the right initial public surface, with broader consumers added only after the command inventory contract is accepted?


## Draft follow-ups

- [#104158](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104158): live paired-node command collection
- [#104159](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104159): scoped command prompt projection
- [#104160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104160): generated command reference and freshness guard

These remain draft and contract to their feature-only diffs after this foundation merges.

target.title: fix(memory-core): keep same-agent session hits in memory recall under tree visibility (#103732)
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #103732.

`memory_search(corpus=sessions)` returned 0 hits — and unfiltered searches never surfaced session chunks — while `openclaw memory search` returned session results from the same index (reporter: 1133 indexed session chunks).

### Root cause

Only the tool path runs `filterMemorySearchHitsBySessionVisibility` (`extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts`); the CLI (`cli.runtime.ts`) returns raw `manager.search` results. Inside the filter, every hit's resolved session keys are already scoped to the requester's agent (`filterSessionKeysByScopedAgent`), but each key must then pass a `history`-action visibility guard whose **default `"tree"` visibility forbids every session that is not the requester or its descendant** (`src/plugin-sdk/session-visibility.ts` tree branch). A normal main-agent call (`agent:main:main`) therefore drops every historical `sessions/main/<uuid>` transcript — all of them.

### Change

`extensions/memory-core/src/session-search-visibility.ts`: same-agent hits from **authoritative** key resolutions (QMD artifact identity, exact live-stem matches, plain transcript stems) no longer require the per-key history guard — the agent scoping already applied is the boundary that matters for memory recall. Two protections are preserved deliberately:
- **sandboxed runs** keep the strict guard, so the spawned-subtree clamp still holds;
- **lossy QMD slug-fallback resolutions** keep the strict guard, so a slug cannot authorize the wrong transcript (existing regression `does not authorize QMD archived .md hits through lossy slug fallback` still passes).

## Verification

- New regressions (first one confirmed failing on main): same-agent hit under the default tree visibility is retained; the same hit under `sandboxed: true` is still dropped.
- `pnpm test extensions/memory-core` — full plugin suite passed (including all 728-line visibility suite + the lossy-slug security case).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: memory_search tool returns 0 session hits despite an indexed sessions corpus; CLI works.
Real environment tested: the real `filterMemorySearchHitsBySessionVisibility` production filter through its dedicated test harness with a real combined session store shape (`agent:main:historic` transcript, requester `agent:main:main`, default visibility).
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core`
Evidence after fix: the same-agent hit that main drops (tree forbid) is retained; sandboxed and lossy-slug paths still deny.
Observed result after fix: corpus=sessions recall returns same-agent transcripts, matching the CLI.
What was not tested: a live gateway with a populated QMD/sqlite index; the divergence is fully reproduced at the filter boundary that separates the tool path from the CLI path.

target.title: fix(agents): prioritize skill-creator over direct skill_workshop calls for skill creation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #104104

The model non-deterministically routes between invoking the `skill-creator` skill and calling the `skill_workshop` tool directly when a user requests skill creation. This happens because the system prompt presents two competing, unprioritized directives at the same level:

1. **Skills section** — lists `skill-creator` and instructs the model to load it when applicable
2. **Skill Workshop section** (`skill-workshop-prompt.ts`) — unconditionally directs: "Route durable skill work through `skill_workshop`"

When `skill_workshop` is chosen directly, the `skill-creator` workflow (validation rules, structure conventions, edit workflow) is bypassed entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Skill Workshop prompt section now includes explicit routing priority: "When the `skill-creator` skill is available, load it first — it owns the creation workflow and will route to `skill_workshop` when ready." This establishes a single unambiguous routing path: user request → `skill-creator` → `skill_workshop`.

The change is a one-line edit to `skill-workshop-prompt.ts` with no function signature changes, no new parameters, and no caller modifications. When `skill-creator` is unavailable, the directive becomes a natural no-op.

## User Impact

Users creating skills via chat will consistently get `skill-creator`'s structure and validation guidance before the proposal reaches `skill_workshop`, resulting in higher-quality skill proposals.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts` — 94/94 pass (including "instructs models to use skill_workshop only when the tool is available")
- Change: 1 file, 1 line (`src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts:11`)

target.title: fix(mcp): fix-mcp-cli-oauth-login-timeout
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running `openclaw mcp login <name>` could see the OAuth login workflow hang indefinitely when the MCP server, OAuth discovery endpoint, or an upstream proxy stopped responding during the CLI login flow.

Before this patch, `mcp login` built an HTTP `fetchFn` for `runMcpOAuthLogin(...)` but did not apply the configured MCP `requestTimeoutMs` to those OAuth HTTP calls. A stalled remote endpoint could leave the login command waiting forever with no deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fix scoped to the explicit CLI OAuth login workflow: pass `resolved.requestTimeoutMs` from `mcp login` into `runMcpOAuthLogin(...)` as `fetchTimeoutMs`, then wrap the login-only `fetchFn` with `wrapFetchWithTimeout` so OAuth HTTP requests abort with `TimeoutError` after the configured deadline. This does not widen timeout behavior to the broader MCP runtime transport layer.

## User Impact

**Before:** `openclaw mcp login` could hang forever on a non-responding OAuth/discovery endpoint even when the MCP server had a configured timeout.

**After:** Configured MCP `requestTimeoutMs` values apply to CLI OAuth login HTTP requests; stalled endpoints abort instead of blocking the operator indefinitely.

## Evidence

- `src/cli/mcp-cli.ts:1257` — `mcp login` forwards `fetchTimeoutMs: resolved.requestTimeoutMs`
- `src/agents/mcp-oauth.ts:41` — `wrapFetchWithTimeout` aborts hung OAuth fetches with `TimeoutError`
- `src/agents/mcp-oauth.ts:281` — login attempt wraps `fetchFn` before MCP SDK `auth(...)`
- `src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts` — `configures enablement, timeouts, and OAuth login` asserts `fetchTimeoutMs: 9_000`
- `src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts` — `applies the configured fetch timeout to OAuth HTTP requests`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** CLI MCP OAuth login no longer leaves OAuth HTTP requests unbounded when the remote endpoint stops responding; configured login timeouts now abort with `TimeoutError`.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Operator runs `openclaw mcp login <name>` → `registerMcpCli` login handler → `resolveMcpTransportConfig` reads `requestTimeoutMs` → `runMcpOAuthLogin({ fetchTimeoutMs, fetchFn })` → `wrapFetchWithTimeout` → MCP SDK `auth(...)` OAuth HTTP fetch receives an `AbortSignal` that fires at the deadline.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; production `runMcpOAuthLogin` / `wrapFetchWithTimeout` and `mcp login` wiring exercised via colocated Vitest on branch `codex/mcp-login-timeout` (commit `f3ed549a13f`). No live stalled OAuth server in this environment.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Uses `resolveTimerTimeoutMs` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/number-coercion` to clamp timeout input; provider constraints N/A because this is CLI-local OAuth login HTTP wrapping, not model-provider routing.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node 22, source checkout on branch `codex/mcp-login-timeout` (head `f3ed549a13f`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts -t "applies the configured fetch timeout" --reporter=verbose
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts -t "configures enablement, timeouts, and OAuth login" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ MCP OAuth provider > applies the configured fetch timeout to OAuth HTTP requests 6ms
   pending OAuth fetch after 25ms => { ok: false, error: TimeoutError }
   runMcpOAuthLogin({ fetchTimeoutMs: 25 }) => "authorized"
   baseFetch called with AbortSignal

 ✓ mcp cli > configures enablement, timeouts, and OAuth login 680ms
   runMcpOAuthLogin called with fetchTimeoutMs: 9000
   (from `mcp configure docs --timeout 9` then `mcp login docs --code abc123`)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** A hung OAuth fetch aborts at the configured deadline with `TimeoutError` instead of waiting indefinitely; `mcp login` forwards the configured MCP timeout (`9_000` ms for `--timeout 9`) into `runMcpOAuthLogin`.
- **What was not tested:** Live `openclaw mcp login` against a real stalled OAuth/discovery endpoint; broader MCP runtime/session transport timeouts (explicitly out of scope for this PR).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

---

Related to #103089

---

## Current-Head Gateway Proof (HEAD 9b2e033)

**Environment:** Linux 4.19.112, Node v22.19.0, commit \`9b2e03390f8'
**Method:** Real Gateway session handlers (gateway-server project)

### Seed sessions:
- \`"main"\` — owned by pluginA
- \`"user"\` — ownerless (user session)
- \`"self"\` — owned by pluginB

### Proof: 11 scenarios on current HEAD

```
━━━ 1. Seed sessions: pluginA(main), ownerless(user), pluginB(self) ━━━
  ✓ Seed data ready

━━━ 2. Ownerless existing-target rejection ━━━
  ❌ take over ownerless "user" by key

━━━ 3. Foreign-owned existing-target rejection ━━━

     → Plugin "pluginB" cannot take over session "agent:main:main" because it did not create it.

━━━ 4. Plugin can create NEW session (non-existent key) ━━━

     → child owner: pluginB

━━━ 5. Cross-plugin fork rejection ━━━
  ❌ fork pluginAs session

━━━ 6. Fork from ownerless session rejection ━━━

━━━ 7. Same-plugin parent link (allowed) ━━━
```

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search handled blank or whitespace-only queries too late. The manager could initialize the provider, assert provider state, or bootstrap search work before the preflight returned an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blank query eligibility is a local preflight contract and should not require provider setup. This change shares query normalization with the existing preflight and short-circuits blank queries before provider/bootstrap work.

## User Impact

Whitespace-only memory searches return `[]` cheaply and deterministically, without requiring provider credentials, indexes, or search startup.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`.
- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.ts`.
- Added `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts` proving blank search returns `[]` before provider init, provider assertion, index check, or sync bootstrap.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Controlled manager proof: `node --import tsx - <<'EOF' ...` invoked the actual `MemoryIndexManager.search` method with a whitespace-only query and provider/bootstrap counters.
- Normal manager proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF' ...` constructed a real `MemoryIndexManager` through `MemoryIndexManager.get({ cfg, agentId: "main", purpose: "cli" })`, then ran a whitespace-only search.

## Proof

- Controlled proof query: whitespace-only.
- Controlled proof result: `resultCount: 0`, `results: []`.
- Provider/bootstrap counters all stayed zero: `ensureProviderInitialized: 0`, `assertRequiredProviderAvailable: 0`, `hasIndexedContent: 0`, `sync: 0`.
- Normal manager proof used a temporary workspace/state dir and `provider: "none"` with vector disabled to avoid external provider setup.
- Normal manager proof output:
  - `managerConstructed: true`
  - `purpose: "cli"`
  - `blankResultCount: 0`, `blankResults: []`
  - `beforeProviderState` and `afterProviderState`: `{ "mode": "pending", "requestedProvider": "none" }`
  - `beforeFiles: 0`, `afterFiles: 0`, `beforeChunks: 0`, `afterChunks: 0`
- This proves the blank-query preflight returns before provider initialization, provider availability assertion, index checks, or sync bootstrap on both the direct search method and a normally constructed manager path.


## Public CLI Proof

- Public CLI proof command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`, with `<whitespace>` equal to `" \n\t "` in a temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and workspace.
- Config used `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "none"`, `store.vector.enabled: false`, and search/index watchers disabled, so a blank-query preflight must not need any embedding provider.
- Search exit: `0`.
- Search stdout:
  ```json
  {
    "results": []
  }
  ```
- Follow-up status command: `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` in the same fixture.
- Follow-up status core: `provider: "none"`, `requestedProvider: "none"`, `vector.enabled: false`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, `dirty: true`.
- Workspace contents stayed `MEMORY.md` plus `memory/`; only the normal OpenClaw state SQLite files were created under the temporary state dir.
- This proves the public `openclaw memory search` path returns `[]` for a whitespace-only query before provider/bootstrap/index work.

## Required Provider CLI Comparison
Current-main baseline: `upstream/main@fab69517b3`. PR head: `a7cc3fc2096915f8956c529193bb32d4e6c30bbe`.

I ran the same public CLI command against current main and this PR head with an explicit required remote provider and intentionally absent credentials:

- Command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`
- Environment: `OPENAI_API_KEY` unset, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`
- Config: `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "openai"`, `model: "text-embedding-3-small"`, `fallback: "none"`, `sync.watch/onSessionStart/onSearch: false`, `store.vector.enabled: true`

Redacted output:

```text
upstream/main@fab69517b3
exitCode: 1
stderr: Memory search failed: No API key found for provider "openai" ... | missing-provider-auth
stdout: [ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.

PR head@a7cc3fc209
exitCode: 0
stdout: {
  "results": []
}
stderr: $ node scripts/run-node.mjs memory search --query '<whitespace>' --json
```

The same fixture's `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` output on both revisions reported `provider: "openai"`, `requestedProvider: "openai"`, `vector.enabled: true`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, and `providerState.mode: "pending"`. That confirms this is not `provider: "none"` FTS-only proof: current main reaches required-provider auth before blank-query rejection, while the patched head returns the blank-query `[]` result before provider/bootstrap/index work.

## What Problem This Solves
Existing-session `hover`, `scrollIntoView`, `drag`, `select`, and `fill` actions already run the post-interaction navigation guard, but their success responses kept the pre-action `targetId`. If one of those guarded actions triggered a renderer swap or same-URL target replacement, the next browser action could continue with a stale target.

## Why This Change Was Made
`click`, `clickCoords`, `type`, and `press` already resolve the current target after the same guarded existing-session path. This change applies that same response contract to the remaining guarded non-click interactions without changing unguarded or unsupported actions.

## User Impact
Browser agents using existing-session profiles get the current tab target after guarded hover, scroll, drag, select, and fill interactions. This reduces stale-target follow-up failures after navigation-like page changes.

## Evidence
- Added a regression test that simulates a guarded non-click interaction replacing the old target and verifies the response returns the replacement target.
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.existing-session.test.ts`
- Touched-file checks:

  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.act.existing-session-navigation-guard.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`

## Live Existing-Session Browser Proof
Current head: `e809e5a2f8183fd683b66eabff185fe055d0f43c`.

I ran a local live proof with real Chrome, real `chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, and the real OpenClaw Browser HTTP routes. The proof launched temporary `/usr/bin/google-chrome --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=<redacted>`, started `startBrowserBridgeServer` with an existing-session profile using `cdpUrl: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>` and `ssrfPolicy: { dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork: true }`, then used only public Browser routes:

1. `POST /tabs/open` opened a launcher page.
2. `POST /act` with `kind: "evaluate"` opened a script-owned child tab.
3. `GET /snapshot?format=ai&targetId=<old>` captured refs from the child tab.
4. The child tab opened an same-URL replacement tab and closed itself after the guarded action passed URL stability checks.
5. `POST /act` ran each guarded action, and `POST /act` with `kind: "wait"` used the returned target to prove the next action succeeds.

```text
scrollIntoView: delay=1450 actStatus=200 old=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:11 returned=chrome-mcp:<session>:...:12 replaced=true waitStatus=200 waitOk=true
```

target.title: fix(codex): trigger model fallback on usage-limit promptError (#103734)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex-backed turn hits the subscription usage limit, the Codex harness
returns a `promptError` in the attempt result instead of throwing. The host's
model fallback is throw-driven — it only engages when `FailoverError` is thrown.

The existing prompt-error handler already classifies the error and enters
`resolveRunFailoverDecision`.  However `shouldRotatePrompt` always returns true
for rate/billing limits, so the handler first tries **auth profile rotation** —
retrying the same harness with a different profile.  For harness-owned transports
(Codex) the limit is on the harness session, not the profile, so every rotation
fails identically.  This wastes the user's quota and burns retry budget
before fallback can engage.

Fixes #103734.

## Why This Change Was Made

One 8-line addition in `shouldRotatePrompt` (`failover-policy.ts`): when a
plugin harness owns the transport **and** the failover reason is `rate_limit`
or `billing`, skip profile rotation.  The decision falls through to
`fallback_model` in `resolveRunFailoverDecision`, which throws a `FailoverError`
that the outer fallback loop catches immediately.

Non-harness providers and non-limit errors are unchanged — they still rotate
profiles before falling back.

## User Impact

**Before:** Codex usage limit → profile rotation → all profiles fail →
run budget exhausted or model fallback with wasted quota.

**After:** Codex usage limit → `rate_limit` → skips rotation → falls back
to next configured model immediately.

## Evidence

### Live agent proof (Codex usage-limit → fallback model)

Primary `openai/gpt-5.5` (Codex) forced to return a redacted usage-limit error.
Fallback `zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B` configured.  Run completes on the fallback:

```
$ pnpm --filter openclaw openclaw agent --local \
    --message "say hello in one word" --session-key agent:proof:103734

  stage=prompt decision=fallback_model reason=rate_limit
  from=openai/gpt-5.5

  subscription usage limit.

[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_succeeded
  candidate=zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B

Hello

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Realistic-stream regression** (`processes.stream-errors.test.ts`): `spawn` is mocked to return a child whose `stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` are real `PassThrough` streams, driven through the production `startProcess` entry point. This exercises the real close path, including `finalizeProcess()` calling `stdin.destroy()` and `finalizeExec`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests assert (after fix):**

1. **Stdout error → kill, then finalize via close:**
   - `managed.failure` is set; `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called; `managed.closed` stays `false` and `finalizeExec` has NOT run yet (the error handler does not finalize).
   - After the real `close` event: `managed.closed` becomes `true`, `finalizeExec` runs exactly once with `status: "failed"`, and notifications are ordered `process/exited` before `process/closed`.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, the process stays alive, and `finalizeExec` does not run.

**Note on the prior revision:** the earlier fake child's `stdin` only implemented `end()`, so `finalizeProcess()`'s `stdin.destroy()` threw a `TypeError` that the close path swallowed — `finalizeExec` silently never ran even though the test passed. The `PassThrough` streams fix that: `finalizeExec` is now actually reached and asserted, so the finalization lifecycle is proven end-to-end.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** a live OS-level pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion). The error path itself is exercised exactly — the production handlers registered by `startProcess` receive real stream `error` events and the real close/finalize lifecycle runs to completion.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(browser): apply profile proxy policy to tab list redaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
`/tabs` and `/tabs/action` list redaction only used the global SSRF policy. They did not include the selected profile's browser proxy mode, while tab open/focus/select already use `browserNavigationPolicyForProfile`.

## Why This Change Was Made
Strict browser navigation policy depends on whether the browser profile itself is proxy-routed. Tab list URL redaction is a navigation-result policy check, so it should receive the same profile-aware policy as the other tab routes.

## User Impact
Tab list responses now redact URLs consistently for proxy-routed browser profiles instead of evaluating them with an incomplete policy. This keeps list responses aligned with focus/select safety checks.

## Evidence
- Changed tab list redaction to accept `browserNavigationPolicyForProfile(ctx, profileCtx)`.
- Added route regression coverage for both `/tabs` and `/tabs/action list` passing `explicit-browser-proxy` into result guards.
- Added attach-only route proof in `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts` that uses the real browser route context and real navigation guard: strict SSRF plus `--proxy-server=...` redacts a public IP-literal tab URL for both list endpoints.
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
  - Result: 2 files / 24 tests passed.
- Touched-file checks:
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts`
  - `OPENCLAW_OXLINT_SKIP_PREPARE=1 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts`
  - `git diff --check`
- Autoreview closeout:
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude --prompt '<scope prompt>'`
  - Result: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Proof
The original route regression verifies the policy object passed to the redaction guard. The attach-only regression now exercises the same route handlers with the real navigation guard and a loopback OpenClaw CDP profile configured with `--proxy-server=...`; under strict SSRF, the tab list response keeps the tab identity but blanks the URL for both `GET /tabs` and `POST /tabs/action { action: "list" }`. This proof does not require a live proxy or credentials because the changed behavior is the preflight navigation-result policy decision before any browser network request.

target.title: fix(workboard): check active claim before dependency status guard in claim()
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #104050 — `claim()` checks the dependency status guard (card status must be `"ready"`) before checking whether the card is already claimed. Since a successful claim moves the card to `"running"`, any repeat claim on a card with parents returns the misleading error `"card dependencies are not done"` instead of `"card already claimed by <owner>"`.

Cards without parents are unaffected — only the misordered dependency guard triggers this false error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Swap the order of two guards in `claim()`: check the active claim lease before the dependency status guard. The existing claim check (`already claimed by`) and dependency check (`dependencies are not done`) each remain correct on their own; the fix is purely about which one runs first.

No status transitions, no new error messages, no API changes — just moving `existingClaim` above `cardParentIds`.

**Test correction (`fbb9293dc5`):** the regression test first pushed here built the parent link through raw `metadata.links`, which `create()` strips (parent/child dependencies must go through `linkCards`). The child was therefore parentless, the dependency guard never fired, and the test passed with *or* without the fix. It now builds a real dependency via `linkCards` + `promoteReady` and asserts the link and promotion, so it genuinely guards the ordering (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix).

## User Impact

Agents that repeat-claim a dependency-backed card now see the correct `"already claimed by <owner>"` error instead of a misleading `"dependencies not done"` that sends them into dependency-debugging loops.

## Evidence

### Real runtime behavior (SQLite-backed `WorkboardStore`)

Reproduced #104050 end-to-end against a real `node:sqlite` store (not the in-memory test double), driving the public store API — build a parent→child dependency with `linkCards`, mark the parent `done`, `promoteReady`, then claim the child twice. `before` = pre-fix (`HEAD~1`), `after` = this fix.

```
########## BEFORE (pre-fix) ##########
setup   child.parents=[<cardId>] child.status=ready
claim#1 owner=main   -> status=running  token=<redacted>
claim#2 owner=other  -> Error: card dependencies are not done.     # misleading

########## AFTER (this fix) ##########
setup   child.parents=[<cardId>] child.status=ready
claim#1 owner=main   -> status=running  token=<redacted>
claim#2 owner=other  -> Error: card already claimed by main.       # correct
```

<details><summary>Repro driver (throwaway, not committed)</summary>

```ts
import { mkdtempSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { WorkboardStore } from "./extensions/workboard/src/store.ts";
import { createWorkboardSqliteStores } from "./extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.ts";

const s = createWorkboardSqliteStores({
  dbPath: join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wb-")), "workboard.sqlite"),
});
const store = new WorkboardStore(s.cards, {
  boards: s.boards, subscriptions: s.subscriptions, attachments: s.attachments,
});

const parent = await store.create({ title: "Parent A", status: "todo" });
const child  = await store.create({ title: "Child B",  status: "todo" });
await store.linkCards(parent.id, child.id);          // real parent->child dependency
await store.update(parent.id, { status: "done" });
await store.promoteReady();                          // child -> ready

const first = await store.claim(child.id, { ownerId: "main", ttlSeconds: 60 });
console.log("claim#1 ->", first.card.status);        // running
try { await store.claim(child.id, { ownerId: "other" }); }
catch (e) { console.log("claim#2 ->", e.message); }
```

</details>

### Regression test (now effective)

The corrected test fails on the pre-fix guard order and passes after the fix:

```
# new test @ FIXED store.ts
  Tests  1 passed

# new test @ PRE-FIX store.ts (HEAD~1)
  × reports already claimed instead of dependency error for a claimed dependency-backed card
  AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error matching /already claimed/
    but got 'card dependencies are not done.'
```

### Full suite + lint

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  80 passed (80)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts
  exit 0
```

1 production line moved + 1 effective regression test. Bounded to `extensions/workboard/src/`. No config, SDK, CLI, docs, or changelog surface was added.
